title: controlplane-az-affinity-and-dynamic-interface-endpoint-scaling
author: Liam Zhang
release_notes: Deterministic AZ affinity for control plane subnets; autoscaling for interface endpoints to reduce hotspotting; route53 resolver rule improvements for split-horizon; least-privilege SG templates; migration helper for safe rollout and rollback.
description:
Motivation: In some customer VPCs we observed uneven control-plane resource concentration across AZs leading to throughput hotspots and single-AZ exposure during maintenance. This PR introduces deterministic AZ affinity for control-plane subnet allocation and a small control-plane interface-endpoint autoscaler so ENIs and private DNS endpoints scale with controlled upper bounds. It also hardens security groups and adds Route53 Resolver rule scaffolding for split-horizon DNS during migrations.

Summary of changes: commits: 1) add az_affinity hashing algorithm and terraform module (redwood_private.controlplane.az_affinity) that maps account+region+environment to AZ selection weights; 2) implement endpoint_autoscaler module that deploys a small predictable autoscaling group for aws_interface_endpoint ENIs (configurable min/max and cooldowns) plus CloudWatch metrics and a Lambda scaler; 3) update controlplane subnets to expose explicit az_index and reuse deterministic naming for stable IP allocations; 4) introduce route53_resolver_conditionals to create conditional forwarding rules and resolver rules for split-horizon migrations; 5) add least-privilege security group templates (controlplane-sg, endpoint-sg) and IAM role adjustments for autoscaler Lambda; 6) add migration helper scripts (scripts/migrate-az-drain.sh and scripts/rollback-endpoint-state.sh) and docs; 7) small helm/values change to private-installer chart to surface endpoint autoscaling flags.

Files changed (high level): terraform/modules/controlplane/subnets.tf, terraform/modules/controlplane/variables.tf, terraform/modules/controlplane/outputs.tf, terraform/modules/controlplane/az_affinity.tf, terraform/modules/endpoint_autoscaler/main.tf, terraform/modules/endpoint_autoscaler/iam.tf, terraform/modules/endpoint_autoscaler/lambda_scaler.py, terraform/modules/sg/templates/controlplane_sg.tpl, terraform/modules/route53/resolver.tf, charts/private-installer/values.yaml, scripts/migrate-az-drain.sh, docs/private-installer/upgrade-endpoint-scaling.md

Key implementation notes: - AZ affinity: deterministic algorithm uses FNV-1a hash over account_id|region|env and maps to AZs weighted by availability zone counts in the region. This keeps allocations stable across apply cycles while allowing explicit overrides for customers who opt into manual AZ mapping. - Endpoint autoscaler: implements conservative scaling driven by a custom CloudWatch metric (EndpointActiveFlows) aggregated from the service side; autoscaler uses a Lambda to reconcile desired ENI count against Terraform-managed interface endpoints so we avoid uncontrolled drift. Configs expose min/max/target. - DNS: Route53 Resolver rules are created with conditional forwarding to customer DNS where provided. We also add resolver rule tags to enable clean teardown during rollbacks. - Security: SG templates shift from broad CIDR allowances to service-specific ports and internal ALB/worker ranges; added notes on audit logs and flow logs. - Rollout plan: default behavior is opt-in via values.enable_endpoint_autoscaler=false. When enabling, operator runs scripts/migrate-az-drain.sh which drains control-plane nodes in a canary AZ, verifies endpoint autoscaler scales ENIs appropriately, then proceeds region-wide. Rollback instructions are in docs and scripts/rollback-endpoint-state.sh which imports previous terraform state and restores autoscaler min/max to previous values.

Commits (high-level): - 3a2f9b1 add az_affinity module and tests - 5d4c111 implement endpoint_autoscaler with lambda scaler - 7b8e2f0 update controlplane subnets to use az_index and stable naming - 9c1a7bd add resolver rule scaffolding and docs - d4f0b23 add security group templates and IAM policy adjustments - f7e3c44 add migration scripts and helm values toggle

Review conversation (high level): - Ava Patel: "Please add unit tests for the az_affinity mapping and document the failure modes when AZ counts change/reduce." (author) Reply: "Added table-driven unit tests and explicit mapping fallback to first-available AZ; documented behavior in module README." - Diego Liu: "Concerned about Lambda scaler IAM scope." Reply: "Narrowed permissions to only Describe/Modify ENIs and CloudWatch PutMetricData; included sts:AssumeRole constraints for cross-account use." - Monica Reyes: "How will this affect existing on-prem installs?" Reply: "Default is opt-in for autoscaler; az_affinity will not change existing subnet allocations unless operator runs the migration helper. Added helm/values flag to prevent accidental flips." - CI observed one flaky integration test (integ/private-installer-networking) on the first run; terraform-validate initially failed due to a missing variable default and was fixed in 5d4c111; final CI: all checks passed after rerun.

Testing and CI: Ran unit tests for az_affinity (go test), terraform validate and fmt in CI, module-level acceptance tests in a sandbox VPC, and integration smoke tests for private-installer chart. Observability: added metrics for EndpointAutoscaler.DesiredENIs and EndpointAutoscaler.ActiveENIs.

Migration and rollback notes: - Operators should enable the feature in a single non-production region first. Run scripts/migrate-az-drain.sh which will: create a canary subnet with deterministic AZ affinity, cordon/drain nodes in the canary AZ, enable autoscaler for associated endpoints, verify scaling, then proceed. - For rollback: run scripts/rollback-endpoint-state.sh which resets autoscaler bounds and reconverts Terraform state to previous module versions; also provided CLIs for importing interface_endpoint resources if drift occurs.

Backward compatibility and safety: az_affinity is additive and will not rename existing subnets unless operator explicitly migrates. Endpoint autoscaler is opt-in. Security changes are scoped to new SG templates and default to the prior, permissive templates until operator applies the templates.

Merge: squash and merge after approvals from Ava and Diego; changelog and release notes updated.

Follow-ups: - Add telemetry for per-AZ allocation ratios (ENG-1722) - Cross-account endpoint autoscaling checklist for MSP customers - Expand autoscaler to support scaling by request latency in addition to active flows

If you want to test this locally: see docs/private-installer/upgrade-endpoint-scaling.md for a step-by-step example and a small demo harness that runs the lambda scaler against a mock EndpointActiveFlows metric.
notes: Merged after CI green and approvals. No further action required in main branch; customers must opt-in to enable autoscaler.
